Have Got to for What Is Necessary
Have got to represents the idea that something is necessary and a must.

When you use have got to, you are saying that something has to be done and there is no other possible action to take in the present time.

This is the structure you are going to follow:
Subject + have/has + got to + verb (base form) + complement.

For example:
Functional requirements have got to show the behavior of the system.
Business requirements have got to illustrate the objectives or visions of the system.
I have got to find someone who can tell me about the topic the teacher covered yesterday.
The last thing you have got to know about yesterday's class is the domain requirements.
Requirements Measures
Each system or software project that is developed has to be measured. Its metrics help software organizations to keep important information of what they produce.

There are some elements that are considered to be the most important metric systems that a software organization can carry on with their projects.

PRODUCT SIZE
The most essential metric has to deal with the amount of requirements which contain valuable information on the way the system should behave in certain situations. The size of the product is obtained by analyzing such elements like the overall effort, time and money that it took to develop the complete system. Furthermore, aspects of the non-functional requirements, such as safety and the general parameters that the system has to accomplish have to be included within the product size estimation.

REQUIREMENTS QUALITY
Having an objective report of the quality of the requirements provides useful data to the software organizations. Information about the defective, unnecessary, unfinished and missing requirements on past projects reflect the inner flaws of the organization by reporting the logistic and technical issues that have to be addressed during the stages of design, coding and testing.

Once the information that was collected is analyzed, it can be grouped into two different categories: Efficiency and effectiveness. The first one, making reference to the average number of flaws detected during the inspection process reflecting the cost that finding defects has. On the other hand, effectiveness makes reference to the amount of flaws detected in the final product during the inspection stage, reflecting how good this stage is being performed.

REQUIREMENTS STATUS
Keeping track of the status of the projects' requirements is vital to determine the progress it has. Different status give information about the level of completion of the project: Rejected, deleted, deferred (to be implemented in the future), verified (passed all the different tests after its integration), implemented, approved, and proposed (it was recommended by someone).

REQUEST FOR CHANGES
The record of any type of modification or change in the project's requirements provides information on the way these are addressed. The amount of changes, the moment that those were found and proposed and the time it took to implement them provide an insight of all the organs that intervene in the creation of the project and can show what processes in which branches of the organization need to be revised.

EFFORT
Knowing how much effort it took employees to successfully complete a project can give important evidence for future projects.

images.text:
Jessica: Hi, Steven. I have got to find someone who can tell me about the topic the teacher covered yesterday.
Steven: The teacher talked about the requirements measures. You might want to understand this subject thoroughly before next class.
Jessica: Requirements, what?
Steven: The requirement measures. All software organizations had better keep track of the statistics of the products they produce as they provide important information that can improve and strengthen the production phases of future projects. You might want to check out different metric systems such as product size, which assesses time, money, speed and portability; the requirements status, which indicates the level of achievement of the requirements; the request for changes, and effort.

Jessica: Now that I think about that, the quality requirements are also important within those metric systems. Their correct implementation is going to have to provide objective data about the faulty requirements, highlighting those that were defective, unnecessary, and unfinished. Software organizations ought to analyze these pieces of information as they unveil the difficulties that the different areas of the company are presenting. Furthermore, we ought to obtain, from these reports valuable information related to the costs that flaws represent to the company.

Steven: That is correct. The last thing you have got to know about yesterday's class is the domain requirements. They basically display, in specialized terminology, the application domain of the system; in other words, the environment in which the system runs. Finally, they had better indicate the basics of the application domain in order to make the system work in correspondence to its goals.
Jessica: Thank you for the class update. I am going to have to invite you for a coffee after all this help.
